messages:
sophia: Heads-up — after the streaming rollout yesterday our OTLP span volume spiked ~4x for prod. Dashboard alerts went off. We need a short-term retention plan that won't break queries for on-call or cost the infra team a fortune.

devon: saw that. most of the extra spans are tiny heartbeat spans from internal sdk v2. Could we apply a runtime filter to drop spans <10ms and add a production sampling slope? :thinking_face:

kai: runtime filtering helps but be careful: we still need those short spans for p99 latency debugging on RPCs. Maybe filter by span.name prefix like internal/heartbeat and keep service spans.

maya: +1 to prefix filter. Also we should tag env for every span at ingestion so downstream tiering can do TTL by env/service. Right now some spans miss env and end up in prod cold bucket forever.

elisabeth: Cost numbers from infra: extra 4x = ~1200GB/day more. Cold storage ops + query latency increase is the main driver. We can do a two-week hot window for prod, then 90d cold compressed. For non-prod, 7d hot, 30d cold. Thoughts?

sophia: That matches my gut. But product wants 30d searchable traces for prod for troubleshooting. If hot window is 14d they lose older fast queries. Could we implement a fast index for 30d using compacted traces (only root+error spans) and full traces in cold? That would keep cost down and allow some search.

devon: technically doable if we store a projection: error/root-span index + span fingerprints. Query path would check projected index for 30d then pull full trace from cold if needed (slower). Implementation work: exporter needs to emit a compacted document to indexer on write.

kai: how about sampling policy? proposal: prod default 1.0 for user-facing services for first 7d, then geometric decay to 0.1 by day30 for noisier services. Non-prod default 0.2. Also allow per-service override via config in the console.

maya: per-service override in console is mandatory. SRE/Support need to pin sampling for certain services during incidents. UX: add a toggle + percent slider and history of changes with who toggled it.

elisabeth: re: backfill — if we change sampling now, we can't reconstruct prior spans. Are we okay with partial historical coverage? Product might request a backfill for a customer incident window.

sophia: backfill path options: 1) replay raw OTLP if we kept it in hot for extra time (expensive). 2) rely on app logs + traces join via trace_id to rebuild partial traces. 3) refuse backfill except for retention-preserved ranges. We need policy and cost estimate table.

trace-bot: auto-note: incident-1234 created because of span_volume_alert. Links: https://intra.redwood/infra/incidents/1234

devon: quick OTEL collector config sketch for prefix drop + export of compact doc:

```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}

processors:
  span-deduper:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: env
        action: insert
        value: ${ENV}
  filter:
    span_names:
      deny: ["internal/heartbeat", "sdk/ping"]

exporters:
  otlp/ingest:
  compact-indexer:
    endpoint: http://indexer:9200

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes, filter]
      exporters: [otlp/ingest, compact-indexer]
```

kai: Nice. One addition: the compacted index should include tags: trace_id, root_service, error_flag, sampled_annotations. That makes 30d lookups useful.

maya: rollout plan suggestion: canary the filter + sampling on 5% of prod traffic for 24h, monitor error budgets, and the traces search SLA. If OK, increase 10x each day until target.

elisabeth: agree. Also add an automated audit job that checks for spans missing env tag and reports top offenders weekly.

sophia: action items:
- devon: prototype collector config and compact doc schema
- kai: sampling slope algorithm + per-service defaults
- maya: console UX mock for sampling slider + override + audit page
- elisabeth: cost model for hot/cold windows + backfill estimates

sophia: tagging this for weekly ops sync. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
